preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain ownership)
Attacker must hold some amount of the CoinToken to execute transfers

violation_target.exploit_hint: As owner, set tax wallets to attacker-controlled addresses, then manipulate buy/sell taxes to high values. Execute trades through Uniswap pair to generate tax revenue that gets sent to attacker wallets. Alternatively, blacklist other users to prevent them from selling while owner dumps tokens. Use setBuyTax() and setSellTax() to set extremely high taxes (up to 100%), then setTaxWallets() to attacker addresses. Trigger trades to collect fees in BNB.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract is a typical tax token with owner privileges. The owner can set buy/sell taxes up to 100% (since denominator = 100) and configure tax wallets. The vulnerability is that the owner can set tax wallets to attacker-controlled addresses and set high taxes, then trigger trades to collect fees in BNB. The contract also has blacklist functionality to prevent others from selling while the owner dumps. The exploit path: 1) Become owner (or impersonate owner), 2) Set tax wallets to attacker addresses, 3) Set buy/sell taxes to high values (e.g., 100% each), 4) Execute a trade (buy or sell) through the Uniswap pair to generate tax revenue that goes to attacker wallets. Since the oracle checks attacker balance increased (NATIVE), we need to ensure the attacker receives BNB from tax distribution.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the owner (or gain ownership via storage slot overwrite), set tax wallets to attacker address, set high sell tax (100%), then sell tokens via the Uniswap pair. The sell will incur 100% tax, which gets collected in the contract and later distributed to tax wallets (attacker). We'll need to trigger the tax swap threshold by selling enough tokens. We'll also need to ensure we have tokens to sell (deal tokens to attacker) and some BNB for gas and possibly for buying. Since we're impersonating owner, we can also exclude ourselves from taxes to avoid paying tax on our own sell? Actually, if we're excluded, no tax is collected. So we should NOT exclude ourselves. We'll set tax wallets to attacker address for dev, marketing, charity. Then sell tokens, causing 100% tax to be taken, which will be swapped to BNB and sent to attacker wallets.

We can find the slot and overwrite. But easier: we can impersonate the current owner. We'll need to know the owner address. Could be from constructor: _setOwner(_addr[5]). We can fetch via call. But for PoC, we can assume we can impersonate the owner via vm.prank with the owner address. We'll need to get owner address via a call to owner() function. 2. Set tax wallets (dev, marketing, charity) to attacker address (address(this)). 3. Set sell tax to 100% for all components (dev, marketing, liquidity, charity). Note denominator = 100, so 100 means 100%. 4. Ensure we have tokens to sell: deal tokens to attacker (since we are not excluded, we need tokens). 5. Sell tokens via Uniswap pair (transfer to pair) to trigger tax. The tax will be collected in contract and when threshold reached, swapped to BNB and sent to attacker wallets. 6. We need to ensure swap threshold is met: swapThreshold = 0.0000005 ether (5e11 wei). We'll sell enough tokens to exceed that in tax. 7. After selling, we may need to call triggerTax() to force distribution if threshold not met? Actually handleTax will check ethValue >= swapThreshold. We'll ensure we sell enough. 8. Finally, check attacker BNB balance increased.
